exhibit many signs of mourning. From last Saturday,

had their flags half mast high, and a few of the
inhabitants employed under Government, including
the Post-office, put up shutters, or otherwise showed
their regard for the Sovereign's loss.

triennal visit ofthe Associated Independent ministers

public tea on the occasion, and a meeting presided over
by the Rev. W. M. Fell, pastor of Chesil Chapel, the
deputation being the Rev. U. B. Randall, of Beamin¬
ster, and the Rev. W. R. Waugh, of Lyme.
